_comment: Third-party agent/skill libraries RAR aggregates. Adding a source is a
config edit, not a code change — scripts/crawl_sources.py reads this file.
RAR INDEXES, IT DOES NOT MIRROR. Only catalog metadata is stored (name,
description, tags, author, link, and any counts the source itself
publishes). Skill bodies, bundles and source files are never copied into
this repo — every item links back to the origin. That keeps aggregation on
the same footing as a search index rather than a redistribution, which is
what makes it safe to do across sources whose licenses differ or cannot be
read. `license` below records what we could actually verify, and
`license_verified: false` means exactly that — unknown, so treat as
all-rights-reserved and never republish content from it.

sources.license_note: The GitHub repository is behind organization SAML enforcement, so the LICENSE file cannot be read programmatically. The Pages site and skills.json are publicly served. Index-only: metadata and links, never content.

sources.publisher: Sean Galliher and Cowork Cookbook contributors
sources.license_note: Recipe content is CC BY 4.0 and code is MIT. RAR remains index-only: it stores normalized metadata and attribution, then generates its own callable method from that metadata without copying recipe prompts or bundles.
